hints: Focus on what makes a carbon chiral, it must be sp3 and joined to four completely different groups.
Look closely at the middle three carbons, $\text{OCH}_2-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}_2\text{O}$, and list the four groups on the central $\text{CH}$.
Check if the left and right sides of that central carbon are really different or just mirror images of the same chromone unit.
walkthrough:
**Recall the test for chirality**

A chiral centre is a carbon with four single bonds to four different atoms or groups. If even two groups are the same, it cannot be chiral.

Rule:
$$\text{chiral C = sp}^3 \text{ carbon with 4 different substituents}$$

**Ignore the flat parts**

Most of this molecule is aromatic rings and $\text{C=O}$ and $\text{C=C}$ bonds. Those carbons are sp2 and flat, so they can never be chiral centres.

Only possible candidates are the three sp3 carbons in the linker:
$$\text{-OCH}_2-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}_2\text{O-}$$

**Test the two $\text{CH}_2$ carbons**

Each $\text{CH}_2$ is bonded to one O, one C, and two H atoms. Because it has two identical H atoms, it fails the test immediately.

$$\text{CH}_2 \text{ has 2 x H, so not chiral}$$

**Test the central $\text{CH(OH)}$ carefully**

This carbon looks promising at first. It is bonded to $\text{-OH}$, $\text{-H}$, $\text{-CH}_2\text{O- (left)}$, and $\text{-CH}_2\text{O- (right)}$.

But the molecule is symmetrical. Both the left $\text{-CH}_2\text{O-chromone}$ and the right $\text{-CH}_2\text{O-chromone}$ groups are identical.

$$\text{central CH has two identical CH}_2\text{O-chromone groups, so not chiral}$$

**Conclude the count**

No carbon has four different groups, so there are zero chiral centres in disodium cromoglycate.

options.A: Correct. The two $\text{CH}_2$ groups have two H atoms each, and the central $\text{CH(OH)}$ has two identical $\text{CH}_2\text{O}$-chromone arms due to symmetry. No carbon meets the four-different-groups rule, so the total is 0.
options.B: Incorrect. This counts only the central $\text{CH(OH)}$ as chiral because it has OH, H and two carbons. The trap is forgetting to check if those two carbon arms are different, but here they are identical, so it is achiral.
options.C: Incorrect. This often comes from counting the two $\text{CH}_2$ carbons or thinking both sides create chirality. $\text{CH}_2$ carbons can never be chiral because they carry two H atoms.
options.D: Incorrect. This counts all three carbons in the $\text{OCH}_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{O}$ linker as chiral. It ignores both the two H atoms on each $\text{CH}_2$ and the symmetry that makes the central carbon achiral.
